speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing hand tremors and recent memory issues; to begin our evaluation, how long have these symptoms been present, and is the tremor rhythmic or intentional?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; since the tremor began in just one hand and is worsening over a year alongside memory loss, have you noticed any stiffness or slowness in his movements? Also, does the tremor seem to get worse when he tries to hold a position or touch an object, or is it more noticeable when his hands are at rest?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Resting tremor worse on the left hand. I also have Soft speech, Reduced facial expressions, Memory decline, Difficulty in managing finances.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Parkinson's Disease with early cognitive impairment.

The classic presentation of a unilateral resting tremor, progressing to include bradykinesia (soft speech, reduced facial expressions), and executive dysfunction (financial difficulties) is highly specific. Given the 1-year history and asymmetric onset, we have sufficient clinical evidence for this diagnosis. I recommend a DAT-SPECT scan to confirm the presynaptic dopaminergic deficit and rule out atypical parkinsonism.
